target.title: fix(agent-core): avoid a crash when empty output has a negative line limit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers using the agent-core truncation helper would see a crash when empty output is evaluated with a negative line limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The head-truncation path now handles empty input before calculating first-line bytes and returns the existing structured truncation result. Valid non-empty truncation behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Agent-core consumers now receive truncation metadata instead of an exception for this empty-output boundary case.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: `truncateHead` no longer throws for empty output with negative line or byte ceilings when called through OpenClaw's session-tool truncation facade.
- Head: `8ed74057b1253f2740186d334bd7ac82299b947f`
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` importing `truncateHead` from `src/agents/sessions/tools/truncate.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/harness/utils/truncate.test.ts` (9 passed)
  - `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
  - GitHub CI for this head is passing, including `build-artifacts`, `check-lint`, `check-test-types`, and compact Node shards.
- Observed runtime result:

```text
head=8ed74057b1253f2740186d334bd7ac82299b947f
empty + negative maxLines
{
  "content": "",
  "truncated": true,
  "truncatedBy": "lines",
  "totalLines": 0,
  "totalBytes": 0,
  "outputLines": 0,
  "outputBytes": 0,
  "firstLineExceedsLimit": false
}
empty + negative maxBytes
{
  "content": "",
  "truncated": true,
  "truncatedBy": "bytes",
  "totalLines": 0,
  "totalBytes": 0,
  "outputLines": 0,
  "outputBytes": 0,
  "firstLineExceedsLimit": false
}
```
